note: Rogers/Shaw business phone bill -- the second anchor for the vendor-driven bill_type rule, and the one that demonstrates the routing win. CU classifies it 'commercial' on 5/5 replicates and the commercial bucket makes po_or_job_number critical, which a telecom bill never carries, so before this change it routed REVIEW_B4_CRITICAL_FIELD. field_policy.vendor_bill_type_override flips bill_type to municipal in code, which drops the PO and GST requirements, and the bill now reaches HAPPY_PATH_CANDIDATE on 5/5. || IMPORTANT -- why the Shaw spellings are in the allowlist: the resolved vendor_name is 'Shaw Cablesystems' (stable 5/5), NOT any Rogers spelling. The payment slip prints 'Please make your cheque payable to Shaw Cablesystems' and vendor_name_extract is told to read the payable-to line first, so the letterhead 'ROGERS BUSINESS together with Shaw' and the page-3 'issued by Rogers Communications Canada Inc.' both lose. Rogers acquired Shaw but still bills under the Shaw brands; dropping 'shaw cablesystems' from _MUNICIPAL_VENDOR_EXACT would make this document stop matching, which is exactly the regression this sidecar exists to catch. || The vendor twins here are closer to flipping than the stable resolved value suggests, which is why the override reads the raw twins as well: extract 'Shaw Cablesystems' is a flat 0.785 on 5/5, while generate returns a bare 'Shaw' at 0.417 on 4/5 and 0.725 on 1/5. The two AGREE (one contains the other), so _prefer_vendor_generate falls through to the confidence tiebreak, and a generate twin edging past 0.785 would resolve vendor_name to 'Shaw' -- deliberately absent from the allowlist, being a surname -- silently reverting bill_type to commercial. A 0.06 margin sits inside CU's documented +-0.3 confidence noise, so the rule is made independent of that tiebreak rather than trusted to it. || invoice_number '260901_rogers' is the SharePoint filename fallback (source 'filename', defaultedFields, 5/5) -- it fires only because the municipal bucket makes invoice_number critical; the document prints no invoice number, only the account 014-2467-8396. || All five narrative fields are asserted '' because build_write_values blanks them for the municipal bucket; diagnosis_solution was UNSTABLE before this change (4 of 5 replicates invented 'The invoice billed monthly business phone service for two phone lines.', 1 returned ''), so the bucket gate is what makes it deterministic. || service_address 'ELECT-8631 ALEXANDRA RD RICHMOND, BC' is the printed SERVICE ADDRESS block, read by the extract twin on 5/5; 'ELECT-' is a Noble site code, the same shape as fortisbc's 'HSE-8667 Cartier St'. || amount_excluding_gst 70.51 verified by arithmetic (73.81 - 3.30). billing period 01-Sep-26 to 30-Sep-26 is printed on the summary. Verifiable absence: po_or_job_number ''. || number_of_days is asserted '' because the bill prints no day count and both twins return nothing; build_write_values writes '' rather than deriving an integer from the period span. The period dates themselves resolve from the printed '01-Sep-26 to 30-Sep-26'. || sub_bill_type 'other' on 5/5: the municipal path takes the classified label and only gas/electric/water/propertytax/business_license are accepted, so a telecom bill lands on 'other'. Worth noting the service address begins 'ELECT-' and CU did NOT mistake that for an electricity account. || folio_number ADDED 2026-09-09 with the new folio twins (commercial-narrative-v20). It is a critical field on property tax notices only (field_policy.PROPERTYTAX_DELTA), and is asserted on every sidecar -- the value on a tax notice, "" everywhere else -- so a regression that starts populating it on ordinary invoices is caught. || invoice_description ASSERTION REMOVED 2026-09-09 (user authorised). It rewords between runs ('Business phone service' / '...services'), and this was the ONLY sidecar of 52 asserting the field -- every other one excludes it under the standing free-text rule first recorded on recommend_240124_0001. Asserting it here was an oversight when this sidecar was scaffolded. || vendor_name ACCEPTS FOUR NAMES, separated by ' || ' (two since user 2026-09-10; set to these four by user 2026-09-13): 'Shaw Cablesystems' (the cheque payable-to line), 'Rogers Communications Canada Inc.' (the page-3 issuer), 'ROGERS BUSINESS' (printed as part of the logo 'ROGERS BUSINESS together with Shaw') and 'ROGERS' (printed only inside longer names and the domain rci.rogers.com, not on its own). Every option is on _MUNICIPAL_VENDOR_EXACT, so any name this sidecar accepts is one the vendor rule books as municipal -- the vendor_name and bill_type assertions cannot contradict each other. Deliberately NOT accepted, although printed: 'Shaw' ('For now, you will continue to pay Shaw') and 'Shaw Cable' ('select Shaw Cable as your payee'), which are not on the allowlist, and 'Rogers together with Shaw' (the remit-to line; CU returned it once as the generate twin) and 'ROGERS BUSINESS together with Shaw' (the logo), which were removed from the allowlist by the user on 2026-09-13. A bill written under any of these would be booked commercial and fail bill_type; accepting them here would hide that behind a passing vendor_name. On 2026-09-09 all 12 cached reads returned the payable-to name 'Shaw Cablesystems' (vendor_name_extract 0.785); on the 2026-09-10 live re-roll, same analyzer definition b5b984bc1a88, all 3 returned the page-3 issuer 'Rogers Communications Canada Inc.' (vendor_name_extract 0.885-0.927). With either name the bill writes bill_type municipal and routes HAPPY_PATH_CANDIDATE (3 of 3 reads each day).
